asDecan.p: Astrologers cut each sign into three slices of ten degrees, called decans, each with a planet and a small card of its own. Your Sun is between 10 and 19 degrees of Leo, the middle slice, where the sign has settled in and is at full strength. In the Golden Dawn order that slice belongs to Jupiter. Jupiter has no special dignity in Leo. It's a visitor there, neither helped nor held back, and it takes its colour from the Sun, which rules the sign. What it brings is an appetite for more, more friends, more room, a longer table. The slice before yours is Saturn's, the Five of Wands, where Leo still has to fight for its place. The one after is Mars and the Seven, holding ground that's already been won. Yours is the stretch in between, when the fight's over and nobody's attacking yet. Strength covers the whole of Leo and is still your Sun card. The Six narrows it to your part of the sign.

You tend to assume people are pleased to see you, and most of the time you're right, which only makes the habit stronger. You walk into a friend's fortieth and within ten minutes you've introduced two people who've never met and started a toast nobody asked for. In a team meeting you're the one who says out loud that Priya's numbers were the reason the quarter went well, and you mean it, though you also quite like being the person who said it. When a group chat goes quiet after you've shared good news, a new job, the house you finally bought, you notice, and you'll check it again before bed. Sundays with nothing planned don't sit well with you. By eleven you've rung three people and there's a barbecue at yours, and you've bought enough sausages for twenty.

The gift nobody mentions is what you're like when things are going badly. Anyone can lead a victory lap. You're unusually good at the half-time talk when the team is down by twenty, or the Monday after the big client walked, when everyone's staring at their screens and you're the one who books a table for lunch and gets people talking about what's next. It isn't forced cheer, or not usually. Jupiter is the planet that expects things to get better, and people can hear that you actually believe it. I've seen this in a lot of middle-decan Leos. They're the ones a small business keeps on through a rough year, partly for the work they do and mostly because the place feels less grim with them in it.

Jupiter's weakness is scale, and in Leo it shows up as promising more than a fortnight can hold. You say yes to hosting Christmas, running the school fundraiser and helping your sister move, all in the same stretch, because each one sounded lovely when you said it and you liked being the person who'd do it. Then something gives, and it's usually the least visible thing, your own sleep or the friend you said you'd ring. The card statement goes the same way after a month of rounds and extravagant presents. There's a quieter one too, which people with this decan rarely admit to. When a close friend gets the promotion you'd both gone for, you're first with the champagne, loud and genuinely glad, and then oddly flat for a week, and you don't tell anyone why.

When something goes wrong, your first move is to make it look smaller in public. The business loses its biggest contract, and by that evening you've told everyone it's fine, you've got three leads, it's probably a blessing. Some of that is real Jupiter optimism and some of it is pride that doesn't want the crowd to see a stumble. About a week later the bravado runs out, and it usually runs out at home, where you go quiet and short with the people who never got the upbeat version. They end up feeling shut out of the bad news, which to be honest they have been. Grief can go the same way. You organise the funeral beautifully and fall apart months later over something small. What actually helps is one person you tell the real numbers to early, and permission to cancel the thing you'd promised to host.

You're a proud partner, and it shows. You'll tell a table of strangers how clever your partner is, post the photo from their graduation, turn up to their work do and charm their boss. Plenty of people have never been loved that out loud before, and they like it. Where it snags is that you love in big gestures, the surprise weekend away, the party, and you can be a bit hopeless at the small daily ones, like remembering they hate coriander or noticing they've been tired for a fortnight. Jupiter adds another habit. It likes a crowd, so the anniversary dinner somehow has six friends at it and most weekends there's a guest in the spare room. Some partners love that. Others would quite like you to themselves now and then, and they may have been hinting.

You do well wherever results are public and people are counted on to show up. Sales, teaching, hospitality, events, running a team, any job with a stage in it somewhere, even if the stage is a Monday stand-up. Jupiter in Leo has a knack for being the face of something, and employers work that out quickly and send you to the conference. You're generous with credit, and still, the colleagues who stayed back building the spreadsheet can end up feeling they did the work and you took the bow. Bring them into the pitch meeting and name them in it. Be careful, too, with work that has no audience at all, long solo research or a remote role with nobody to talk to, because you tend to do worse there than your ability would suggest.

At twenty this decan is often the one everyone knows, with the party, the captain's armband, a lot of friends and a lot of plans, and not much sense yet of which of them matter. The applause comes easily at that age and it's hard to tell the real friends from the audience. By the mid-thirties most people with a Sun here have had at least one public setback, a venture that didn't take off, a role they were passed over for, and the ones who come through it tend to get steadier and choosier, with fewer and better commitments. The fifties often bring the Jupiter side forward. Mentoring, sponsoring, handing the wreath to someone else, and a real pleasure in watching a person they backed at thirty end up running the place. The pride is still there, of course.

Pick one thing that matters to you and do it without telling anyone. Finish the chapter, run the distance, clear out the shed, pay off the card. No post, no mention at dinner, and nothing to your partner either, for a full fortnight. Middle-decan Leos usually find the second week harder than the first, because the urge to share it keeps coming back at odd moments, in the car, at a barbecue. Each time it does, notice what you were hoping to hear back.
